gen-audiowide-gf-noto-serif-gurmukhi: Audiowide sets its letters like tiles, round and wiry, with no hairlines anywhere in the alphabet. But Noto Serif Gurmukhi is the one that pays off in text, with a generous x-height and a gradual weight change you notice on close look.
gen-audiowide-gf-noto-serif-hebrew: Noto Serif Hebrew carries a sturdy, tall-bodied lowercase with subtle thick and thin modulation, set against the blocky, futuristic stems of Audiowide. It would read steadily and with authority, line after line.
gen-audiowide-gf-noto-serif-kannada: Audiowide makes every diagonal as stout as every upright, a techy, tile-like display face with tall lowercase. Beside Noto Serif Kannada, with its mild felt-marker swelling, the two feel like machine and manuscript.
gen-audiowide-gf-noto-serif-khmer: Sharp, techy and wholly uniform. Audiowide has no thick-and-thin contrast to slow the eye, while Noto Serif Khmer adds a middle-of-the-road contrast and hairline thinning at the curves, so the two feel like a circuit board beside a printed page.
gen-audiowide-gf-noto-serif-khojki: Noto Serif Khojki keeps short ascenders above big bowls, with a mild stress in the o and e that feels refined and literary. And Audiowide, with its rounded-wire strokes, supplies the futuristic edge that makes that quiet serif look even softer.
gen-audiowide-gf-noto-serif-lao: Futuristic and unadorned, Audiowide holds a constant stroke weight with no sparkle, which is where it does its best work. Noto Serif Lao does the opposite, offering bookish thicks and thins in moderation and a big lowercase height.
gen-audiowide-gf-noto-serif-makasar: Audiowide builds its uppercase from lines of one constant thickness, giving a tile-like, futuristic stamp. And Noto Serif Makasar, with its towering x-height and soft step from heavy to light, lets the short, big heading do the shouting.
gen-audiowide-gf-noto-serif-malayalam: Noto Serif Malayalam gives every small letter a big open counter, with bowls that thin gracefully, against the zero-contrast tiles of Audiowide. Its bookish refinement is the pair's strongest card.
gen-audiowide-gf-noto-serif-np-hmong: Tiled, techy and flat-stroked, Audiowide matches its crossbars to its stems while Noto Serif NP Hmong adds a slight charcoal-like pressure shadow. Its lowercase rises close to cap height, giving a literary read that moves smoothly.
gen-audiowide-gf-noto-serif-oriya: Noto Serif Oriya reads with dignity, its curves a little heavier than its joins and its lowercase nearly as tall as the capitals. Audiowide, with round letters whose rims match the stems, earns its keep big and brief.
